requirements.requirement: Add at least 512 MiB of disk-backed swap on node1 and make it active.
requirements.summary: A fully allocated 600 MiB /swapfile was created, initialized as swap, and shown active with 614392 KiB usable capacity. It remained active after restart.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the added swap activates automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: The fstab entry was validated by a swapoff/swapon -a transition. A subsequent acknowledged node restart changed the boot identity, after which /swapfile was automatically active and kernel boot messages confirmed its activation.

requirements.requirement: Make the new swap preferred over every existing swap area.
requirements.summary: After restart, /swapfile had priority 32767 while the existing /dev/vda3 swap had priority -1; a final assertion compared it against all other active swap areas successfully.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use an implementation compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were unchanged before and after execution. The implementation used native legacy-platform utilities and successfully recovered through reboot without installing or upgrading packages.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct post-restart evidence. The provider restart protocol is strong: it includes a healthy pre-restart swap state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered swap configuration, metadata, capacity, priority, memory state, OS, and kernel.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-service observation is unsupported on this legacy non-systemd platform.

The package-health collector invoked an unsupported yum operation both before and after execution, so package consistency was not independently established; the command trace nevertheless shows no package mutations.
Final probes did not directly inspect whether the fstab backup and restart log were later removed.

operational_hygiene.summary: All material mutations were causally related to creating, configuring, validating, or reboot-testing the swap. The swapoff/swapon validation was bounded and restored immediately. Two small auxiliary files appear to have been left behind: /etc/fstab.pre-antrieb-swap, a prudent safety backup that was not removed, and /var/tmp/antrieb-restart.log, created for the delayed reboot with no recorded cleanup. Their final existence was not directly probed, so the residue assessment is based on their creation and the absence of cleanup. No executor-caused temporary-file, socket, platform, or package-state regression appears in lifecycle observations.
